transition.rationale: The generator derives expected semantics and diagnostics from the TypeScript implementation, covers fewer inputs than the committed output corpus, tolerates missing compiler/emitter modules, and leaves stale outputs in place.
transition.retirement_condition: Replace implementation-derived expectations with independently accepted specification-authored cases, define the complete output set, make missing generator components fatal, and prove clean exact reproduction.

artifacts.description: Historical JSON fixtures consumed by C binding tests.

transition.rationale: The tracked fixture names reflect an older TypeScript-test extraction pipeline, while the documented helper now writes a different fixture family and no exact production command remains.
transition.retirement_condition: Trace every fixture to an accepted source case, restore or replace the exact deterministic producer, and certify the complete expected output set.

artifacts.description: Swift package-resource projection of the historical C compatibility fixture set.
Generated C compile-assertion test skeleton derived from historical JSON fixtures.

transition.rationale: The generator currently targets converted_from_js_test.c rather than the tracked converted_from_js.c path and has no exact reproduction check.
transition.retirement_condition: Reconcile the intended output path, validate the source fixture set, and prove byte-exact deterministic reproduction.

artifacts.description: Archived historical Omega report retained only as transitional compatibility evidence.

transition.rationale: The timestamped report predates structured product certification, is not reproducible, and is no longer generated or accepted as current certification evidence.
transition.retirement_condition: Remove the archived report and registry entry when historical documentation no longer links to the pre-4.0 Omega snapshot.

artifacts.description: Dependency-resolution lockfiles serialized by their owning package managers.

transition.rationale: The family spans several package managers and registry-resolution models; no single offline, version-pinned reproduction command is currently certified.
transition.retirement_condition: Split the family by package manager, pin each serializer, define offline inputs or trusted registry provenance, and prove exact reproduction without treating a lockfile as its own source.

artifacts.description: Release-only Lua rockspec materialized from the checked-in template.

transition.rationale: Release workflow substitution, local version synchronization, and template naming currently disagree about ownership.
transition.retirement_condition: Assign one release generator, test template substitution and filename construction, and certify the packaged rockspec during release-artifact verification.

artifacts.description: Platform-targeted disposable VS Code extension payload containing the canonical Rust kernel and editor projection, authored LSP adapters, and governed runtime resources.

transition.rationale: The payload is intentionally untracked and its clean-checkout certification is expensive. Dedicated full/release-profile and four-platform CI hardgates execute the registered verification command; the generic generated-artifact check currently enforces only checked-in output families.
transition.retirement_condition: Teach the generated-artifact orchestrator to enforce self-cleaning certification outputs without adding the expensive package rebuild to fast local and pull-request generation checks, then promote this candidate without changing its command or content contract.
